sentences.text: Claim petition cannot be dismissed on the ground that the present claim petition should have been filed before the labour Court and not before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal.
It is urged that Tribunal has wrongly dismissed the claim of the appellant.
4. Learned counsel for the respondent No.3 submits that as the injured was the employee of Tanush Shivane.
Therefore, present claim petition should have been filed before the Labour Court and not before the Claims Tribunal.
Therefore, appeal filed by the appellant be dismissed.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
6. Perusal of the record of the case reveals that appellant*/ claimant has filed the claim petition under Section 163 A of the Motor vehicle Act.

7. Section 163 A of the Motor Vehicle Act reads as under:-
"163A. Special provisions as to payment of compensation on structured formula basis --
(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle of the authorised insurer shall be liable to pay in the case of death or permanent disablement due to accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, compensation, as indicated in the Second Schedule, to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be.
Explanation -- For the purposes of this sub- section, " permanent disability " shall have the same meaning and extent as in the Workmen' s Compensation Act, 1923 (8 of 1923).

(2) In any claim for compensation under sub- section (1), the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or permanent disablement in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle o r vehicles concerned or of any other person.

(3) The Central Government may, keeping in view the cost of living by notification in the Official Gazette, from time to time amend the Second Schedule."
8.
Thus, as per provision of Section 163A of the Motor Vehicle Act, claim petition can be filed under the above section only when it relates to death or permanent disablement.
Perusal of the record of the case reveals that present case does not relates to death or permanent disablement due to accident arising out of use of motor vehicle.
Evidently, appellant has not filed any permanent disability certificate and has not examined any doctor.
Thus, in the instant case, it is not established that appellant has suffered any permanent disability on account of injuries sustained in the motor vehicle Act.

sentences.text: Thus, present case does not come within the purview of Section 163 A of the Motor Vehicle Act.
Hence on this ground alone, appellant's claim petition is not maintainable and no award can be passed in favour of the appellant under Section 163 A of the Motor Vehicle Act.
Hence, principle laid down in Jagdish Singh Tomar (supra) and S. Kumar (supra) do not help the appellant in any away.
10. Accordingly, appeal filed by the appellant is dismissed.
